RAJYA SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Tuesday, the February 26, 2002/Phalguna 7, 1923 ( Saka)
————
(Ministries:  Civil Aviation; Commerce and Industry; Finance;  Petroleum
and Natural Gas; Tourism and Culture; Water Resources)
Total number of questions—20
1
Contract engineers in EIL
*1. SHRI GOPALSINH G. SOLANKI:
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM AND
NATURAL GAS be pleased to refer to
answer to Unstarred Question 1802 given
in the Rajya Sabha on the 7th August,
2001, and state:
(a) whether 50 per cent of vacancies/
requirements of management trainees will
be filled on an annual basis from contract
engineers as decided by the Board of
Engineers India Limited (EIL);
(b) if so, the number of contract
engineers who have been recruited/
absorbed by the management of EIL as
on 31st January, 2002 and if not, the
reasons for delay in re-instating these
contract engineers; and
(c) whether Government would absorb
all the contract engineers within a time-
bound programme and if not, the reasons
therefor?
Deposits with commercial banks
*2. SHRI C.O. POULOSE: Will the
Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state:
(a) whether there has been a sharp
decline in deposits  with the scheduled
commercial banks;
(b) whether the fall in deposits is direct
impact of recent decision to cut down the
interest rates on deposits; and
(c) if so, whether Government would
reconsider the interest structure in these
banks in order to attract more deposits?
VRS for Associate Banks of SBI
*3. DR. Y. LAKSHMI PRASAD: Will
the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that various
employees of the associate banks of the
State Bank of India who have submitted
their applications for VRS on 31st March,
2001, have not been considered as
10 per cent of the staff strength despite
clear instructions issued by Government
in this regard;
(b) if so, the details of such employees
whose applications have not been
considered by the banks, bank-wise and
region-wise;
(c) by when the remaining applications
are likely to be considered in view of the
instructions; and
(d) by when V RS policy is likely to be
opened again for the employees?

Scam in Krushi Urban Co-operative
Bank in Andhra Pradesh
*4. SHRI K.M. SAIFULLAH:
DR. Y. LAKSHMI  PRASAD:
Will the Minister of FINANCE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that a fresh scam
of over compensation of some depositors
in Krushi Urban Co-operative Bank in
Andhra Pradesh has come to light;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the action taken against the erring
officials for their involvement in the
scam?
Revision of freight charges by IBP
†*5. SHRI MUNAVVAR HASAN:
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM AND
NATURAL GAS be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that IBP
company had taken a decision to increase
freight charges for the transporters of
Delhi in its meeting held on
29th November, 2001;
(b) if so, since when the said increase
came into effect;
(c) the names and addresses of the
transporters whose freight has been
increased and the outstanding amount paid
to each of them;
(d) the names and addresses of the
transporters whose outstanding amounts
have not yet been paid with details of
outstanding amount of each of such
transporters; and
(e) by when all transporters will be
paid their dues?
Recapitalisation of co-operative banks
*6. DR. ALLADI P. RAJKUMAR:
Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased
to state:
(a) whether the National Bank for
Agricultural and Rural Development
(NABARD) has demanded Rs. 6000
crores for recap italisation of co-operative
Banks to ensure adequate credit flow; and
(b) if so, what is Government's reaction
thereto?
Economic growth
*7. SHRI  SOLIPETA RAMA-
CHANDRA  REDDY:
SHRI  RUMANDLA
RAMACHANDRAIAH:
Will the Minister of FINANCE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government's attention
has been drawn to the news-item
captioned "Economy grew by just 4 per
cent last year" which appeared in The
Times of India dated the 1st February,
2002;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether it is a fact that Government
declared 5.2 per cent growth of economy
during 2000-01 and 6.4 per cent during
1999-2000;
(d) if so, in what manner it has now
been declared only 4 per cent growth and
how far agricultural and other products
were affected during the period; and
(e) the steps being taken by
Government to improve the economy?
Anti-dumping cases

BIRLA: Will the Minister of
COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY be
pleased to sta te:
(a) whether Government have initiated
anti-dumping cases against several foreign
companies during 2001;
